# Results — Study 663 (Hash-Ribbons)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Capriole
Investments' **Hash Ribbons** (Charles Edwards, 2019): when Bitcoin's 30-day hashrate SMA
crosses back above its 60-day SMA, miner capitulation is ending and it's historically been a
strong buy zone. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `9529d5277775` (BTC-USD).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Hashrate path | **hardcoded** month-end curated table (EH/s), identical to sibling study [292-bitcoin-hashrate](../292-bitcoin-hashrate/) (Blockchain.com 7-day-average chart, digitised to round figures), 2014-01 → 2026-05, **linearly interpolated to a daily path** (no network; a named limitation — see below) |
| Real tape | yfinance daily BTC-USD close (4,305 rows), 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-30 |
| Signal rule | SMA(30) of daily hashrate crosses back above SMA(60), kept only if SMA(30) sat below SMA(60) for **≥21 days** immediately before AND raw hashrate fell **≥8% peak-to-trough** during that stretch (the magnitude filter separating genuine miner capitulation from single-digit noise) |
| Execution | signal known at the close of the crossover day; enter BTC at the **next** trading day's close (one-day lag, the study's single documented execution convention); hold 180 calendar days, else cash at 0% |
| Costs | 10 bps one-way × NAV, charged once on entry and once on exit of each holding episode |
| Data quirk (named) | the hashrate path is **interpolated between monthly anchors**, not real daily data — it smooths away day-to-day noise, so a signal's exact calendar day is accurate only to roughly the anchor month, not the session. It does not erase the multi-month capitulation/recovery swings the ribbon targets (2018 bear, 2020 COVID/halving, 2021 China ban, 2022 FTX are all visible at monthly resolution) |

No survivorship on the Signal axis (BTC-USD is a price index of a single asset — its own
"single surviving coin" character is a Bitcoin-wide caveat, not specific to this indicator, and
is named on the Tradability axis below).

## The signal — genuine Hash-Ribbons buy signals, 2014 → 2026

| # | Signal date | Capitulation length | Window | Hashrate decline |
|---|---|--:|---|--:|
| 1 | **2019-02-12** | 105 days | 2018-10-30 → 2019-02-11 | **−19.7%** |
| 2 | **2020-04-30** | 30 days | 2020-03-31 → 2020-04-29 | **−8.1%** |
| 3 | **2020-06-30** | 31 days | 2020-05-30 → 2020-06-29 | **−8.1%** |
| 4 | **2021-08-15** | 89 days | 2021-05-18 → 2021-08-14 | **−43.9%** |

**n = 4 signals in twelve years of tape.** This is the headline honesty check: every number
below is drawn from **four** historical episodes, two of which (#2, #3) sit two months apart in
the same 2020 recovery and are not statistically independent events. No inference below should
be read as more certain than "four data points allow."

## Forward BTC returns after each signal vs the unconditional distribution

| horizon | signal mean | signal median | unconditional mean (sd) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| +30d | **+10.3%** | +9.7% | +5.90% (22.93%) | +0.97 | 0.3076 |
| +90d | **+49.1%** | +32.6% | +21.06% (53.69%) | +1.27 | 0.1358 |
| +180d | **+112.7%** | +122.6% | +51.46% (104.23%) | +1.15 | 0.1278 |
| +365d | **+246.1%** | +233.0% | +146.83% (268.65%) | +0.78 | 0.1815 |

Placebo: 20 seeds × 1,000 draws (20,000 total) of 4 random dates each, mean forward return per
draw; *p* = share of draws whose mean is **at least as high** as the observed signal mean
(right-tailed — the claim predicts an outperformance).

Every horizon is directionally ahead of the unconditional average — Hash-Ribbons buy signals
really have historically preceded above-average BTC rallies — but **no horizon clears *t* ≥ 2**,
and the best placebo result (*p* = 0.128 at 180 days) means a random 4-date draw beats the
signal about **one time in eight**. With only four (non-independent) events, that is squarely
inside the range luck produces.

## Timer vs buy-and-hold

Long BTC for 180 calendar days after each signal (one-day entry lag), cash otherwise (0%), 10
bps one-way × 2 per holding episode; same [first signal → tape end] window for both legs.

| strategy | total return | CAGR | Sharpe | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Hash-Ribbons timer | +769.8% | +34.07%/yr | **+1.10** | 22.4% of the time |
| Buy-and-hold BTC | **+1502.8%** | **+45.65%/yr** | +0.92 | 100% of the time |

4 signals collapse into **3 distinct holding episodes** (the 2020-04-30 and 2020-06-30 windows
overlap and merge — a direct symptom of the tiny, clustered sample). The timer's Sharpe edges
out buy-and-hold (+1.10 vs +0.92) — being invested only 22% of the time, in the "right" 22%,
does buy some genuine risk-adjustment — but it leaves **half the total wealth on the table**
(+770% vs +1,503%) because it sits in zero-yielding cash through most of BTC's most explosive
stretches. The folklore promises a timing edge; on this tape it is a real but small
risk-adjustment trade-off, not a free lunch.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic BTC-like daily-return world with 6 evenly-spaced "signal" windows and a TUNABLE
planted post-signal drift; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (effect = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.27** (sd 1.29), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted effect = +15%/yr post-signal drift (seed 663) | **+4.03** |

The detector recovers a planted effect cleanly. The null's occasional false positive (2/20
seeds crossing \|t\| ≥ 2 by chance alone) is itself an honest lesson: with only ~6 events, even
a **truly null** world can look "significant" one time in ten by luck — exactly the caution
this study applies to the real tape's own *t* = 0.78–1.27. *(A faithful-engine / power check
only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Every horizon (30/90/180/365 days) shows an above-average forward BTC
  return after a Hash-Ribbons buy signal, but no horizon clears **t ≥ 2** (best Welch *t* =
  +1.27 at 90 days) and no horizon's random-date placebo drops below *p* = 0.10 (best
  *p* = 0.128 at 180 days). With **n = 4** historical signals — two of them overlapping — this
  cannot be certified; it is a directionally consistent, statistically unproven pattern.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** A 180-day timer built on the 4 signals shows a genuine Sharpe
  edge over buy-and-hold (+1.10 vs +0.92) but forfeits more than half the total wealth (+770%
  vs +1,503%) by sitting in cash 78% of the time. The whole construction — the 8% decline
  filter, the 21-day capitulation minimum, the 180-day hold — rests on **three** distinct
  historical episodes; changing any one knob would change the signal count.
- **"Beats random buy dates?" — BUSTED.** Directionally ahead of a random-date placebo at
  every horizon, but never below the conventional *p* < 0.05 bar (best *p* = 0.128). Four
  historical episodes are not enough to distinguish "the ribbon knows something" from "BTC
  spent most of 2019-2026 going up, and four random dates in that window usually look good
  too."
